chunks: And Allah has relied upon for the people of this religion the strengthening of the boundary (Hawzah), and the covering of the defect (Awrah),
He who helped them when they were few and could not help themselves, and protected them when they were few and could not protect themselves, the Living who does not die.

Indeed, whenever you proceed to this enemy with your own self, and meet them with your person and suffer defeat, you will not be a refuge for the Muslims beyond the furthest parts of their lands, and there will be no place after you to which they return,
so send to them a warrior, and gather with him the people of experience and sincerity,
if Allah grants victory, then that is what you love; and if it is otherwise, you will be a support for the people and a returning place for the Muslims.
ai.seo_question: What strategic advice did Imam Ali give to Umar ibn al-Khattab regarding leading the Roman campaign personally versus sending a general?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) advises Caliph Umar to delegate the Roman campaign to a seasoned general rather than leading personally, emphasizing the strategic value of preserving the Caliph as a central anchor (rid') for the community. This counsel reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of 'strategic patience' and the preservation of leadership stability, ensuring that even in defeat, the Muslims retain a unifying figure in Medina. The advice underscores the principle that the leader's presence is more critical to morale and continuity than immediate battlefield glory.
